title: How user journeys are modelled
description: Test graph-RAG's ability to explain the journey-session-event structure.
query: How are user journeys structured in this system? What is the relationship between journeys, sessions, and events?

title: How interaction and signal events combine
description: Test graph-RAG's ability to explain the mixin pattern and dual typing.
query: How does the system capture both what happened and what it means? Can a single event carry both types of information?

title: Types of user objections
description: Test retrieval and explanation of the seven objection categories.
query: What types of objections can users raise, and how are they categorised?

title: Summarise the sample journeys
description: Test graph-RAG's ability to retrieve and summarise journey instance data.
query: Summarise the sample user journeys — who were the users, what were they looking for, and what happened?

title: Types of behavioural signals
description: Test retrieval of the signal event class hierarchy.
query: What kinds of behavioural signals can be extracted from user interactions?

title: How interaction data links to product data
description: Test graph-RAG's understanding of cross-ontology references.
query: How does the interaction tracking system link back to the product catalog? Can you trace from a decision event to the actual products involved?
